items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python

In addition, as it has been mentioned in the paper, the Scikit appears to be implemented in high level language, task-oriented interface and it is written in a way to be minimizing the computational efficiency. items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
Large Scale Personality Classification of Bloggers

    This paper compares different ways of representing words in blogs which is used as features to predict the author’s 5-big personalities. 

    I found it quite interesting because the result shows that by categorize bigrams into psychological categories(using LIWC) as features results in the worst prediction, even though these bigrams are meant to be the most relative words to each personality traits. Which according to the paper is assumed to be too broad, I think it may be another reason that bigrams of LIWC are a little bit too formal, while blogs are usually more like spoken language and not in writing.
    
    I’m recently thinking about researching personality under anonymous environment and this paper actually helps a lot

items.name: 林奕汝
items.note:
Large Scale Personality Classification of Bloggers

To classify bloggers personalities, the authors adopt five-factor model of personality traits on a continuous scale: neuroticism(N), extraversion(E), openness to experience(O), agreeableness(A) and conscientiousness(C). They include 3000 bloggers, each of them completed a self-administered on-line personality questionnaire with those five items. After that, researchers got all articles in their blog in the most recent month. Then the data is processed in 8 conditions (2x2x2 features). Features in the consideration are 1) single or bigrams words window size 2) including stopwords or not 3) boolean or frequency scores. They all trained by the LibLinear model. The best condition, also has statistically significant degradation to the baseline, is bigrams-withStopwords-boolean condition.

I'm surprised on what they found, because doing text data preprocessing, instructions usually mention the exclusion of stopwords. However, in this research, they found the best performing features were a combination including stopwords! And out of our common sense, using boolean performs better than the rate of use, which is used widely in text processing. Moreover, the conceptual breadth could be the reason of bad performance for LIWC in classification tasks. Even though we have common dictionary of words, we cannot ensure they are also common on a specific domain. This work discuss on how the best performed features they found can provide a deeper understanding of personality language behavior online.

This article attract my attention from the beginning to the end. I'm impressed how the authors frame their work. Each paragraph is aligned with readers logic. I believe this is a good example for academic writing as well.

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python

Scikit-learn is a powerful Python module for machine learning. It was built on top of the popular NumPy, SciPy, and matplotlib libraries, so many people that already use these libraries will have a familiar feel to it. It is characterized by a clean, uniform, and streamlined API, as well as by very useful and complete online documentation. As one of the open source machine learning libraries, the latest commit in Scikit-learn(https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn) was 9 hours ago and the number of contributors and committers was 981 and 22431 respectively. Therefore, we can see that Scikit-learn has been active up to now.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python

Scikit-learn is powerful and important for solving diverse problems with machine learning specifically because it enables people who are experts in an area they would like to explore using machine learning but not experts in machine learning themselves. The module does this specifically by putting emphasis on things like the ease of use of the programming language (Python), clarity and completeness of documentation, as well as ease of use of the module itself. Having an easy-to-use machine learning toolkit enables experts to use their expertise instead of relying on ML experts who aren't experts in their field, by being able to better perform on tasks such as feature selection. Obviously someone who is more familiar with the topic of interest will be better enabled to select the most relevant and helpful features for the model to be explored.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
Practical Feature Subset Selection for Machine Learning

The theory behind feature subset selection is not only interesting and useful in that it increases performance and accuracy of common machine learning algorithms, but also that it shares some general themes with the practice of factor analysis used in research, sometimes to eliminate factors that may be inappropriate to look at. The paper itself also mentions that the feature subset selection problem is well-known in statistics. Both want to find the set of features collected or available that are the most relevant for examining in the current process.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
Large Scale Personality Classification of Bloggers

I think that one of the valuable contributions of this study is not only that to the applications of machine learning but also the fact that there are findings and insights this exercise led to that are relevant not only in future applications of machine learning but also those in psychology itself. For example, knowing insights such as that stop words, certain types of topics and linguistic features are worth paying attention to when a mental health profession may have to evaluate a patient's personality type on site. It is good to know that contributions gained through machine learning not only have to feed back into machine learning but also add knowledge that can be directly used in other fields.

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
Practical Feature Subset Selection for Machine Learning

    This paper introduce a new method to CFS to reduce features of a data set before inputting them into machine learning algorithms. Reducing the features of a dataset can result in less parameters to train and thus improve the performance of the machine learning model. And by reducing the features, maybe we human can gain more sense of how the features is correlative with others and how them affect the classification result since we now have less features to focus on and we gain the knowledge that these remaining features are considered effective by the machine learning model.

    It seems like CFS still have some problems to solve before it could be a more robust method to use by the time this paper released, I believe there must be some improvement by now. we should consider implement this technic before training our data.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
Practical Feature Subset Selection for Machine Learning

Feature selection is important for machine learning. To produce more accurate and more understandable results, the data which is inadequate, or contains extraneous and irrelevant information should be extracted. 

I had my own experience to work on support vector machine in text mining field. The vector, i.e. dimension, symbolizes the feature of the sentence. With less knowledge of feature selection, we faced the curse of dimensionality at the beginning. So this paper provide an algorithm (CFS) using features’ performances and intercorrelations to guide its search for a good subset of features. Experimental results are encouraging and show promise for CFS as a practical feature selector for common machine learning algorithms.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
Large Scale Personality Classification of Bloggers

Personal blogs are a popular way to write freely and express preferences and opinions on anything that is of interest to the author, and therefore provide a useful resource for investigating personality. Thus, this paper use a very large corpus of blogs to achieve the task of personality classiﬁcation. .To get a better sense of how personality is expressed in the blogs, it explores the best performing features and discuss how these can provide a deeper understanding of personality language behavior online. First, I think that classifying personality only depending on text is limited. However, the accuracies of result range from 84.36% (openness to experience) to 70.51% (neuroticism), making me surprise to the miracle of text mining.

The paper is assumed to be too broad, but I think maybe there exist other reasons, such as different psychological statuses in reality and on the internet, the way of using languages, which depends on different social contexts. This is just a rudimentary research but it can use on digital marketing; trying to find the most suitable blogger and pay to write sponsored posts..

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
Large scale personality classification of bloggers

The study attempted prediction of personality for 3000 bloggers by machine learning. The researchers used the large corpus of blogs and a bigram based feature representation. Then, accuracies between 70.51%-84.36% were obtained. What's more, they tested different features (e.g. stopwords, inverse document frequency) and found that word bigrams with stopwords treated as boolean features yield good results.
In my view, most people act differently online than they do in real life. Thus, it's surprising for me that high accuracies for predicting personality in a large corpus of blogs.

items.name: 李柏翰
items.note:
Practical Feature Subset Selection for Machine Learning

In machine learning, data preprocessing is an important step before we adopt any machine learning model/algorithm to our data. This paper presented a subset selection algorithm to filter out the irrelevant part of the data and select the important subset of data prior to the learning steps.

In most of the machine learning course, there is always a lesson(most of them are taught at the very beginning), data preprocessing, aimed to make the data set clean, like handling the missing data, finding the odds and etc., but few has mentioned about the subset selection skills.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
Practical Feature Subset Selection for Machine Learning

The paper propose a feature subset selection algorithm using features' intercorrelations to clean data. Usually, I only adopt scale normalization and outlier detection to preprocess training data. In my current work, I conduct ANOVA analysis to only take those significant features to build my model. The paper inspires me that I can also analyze the intercorrelations between features to pursuit for a more robust model.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
Large Scale Personality Classification of Bloggers

The work is really interesting and also makes me think of a deep learning method, Word2vec, which is a popular recurrent neural networks that produce word embeddings. In semantic embedding space, the words that have more similar meanings have closer distance of embeddings vectors. Many works have studied this for classifying personality of individuals using a large corpus of twitter. The topic is still popular and there are many open challenges to predict personality of individuals.
